findings.claim: Enabling legacy HTTP sessions without any session-count cap violates the bounded-work constraint by allowing unauthenticated clients to allocate unbounded server-side session state.
findings.evidence: The hunk changes StreamableHttpServerConfig from `.with_legacy_session_mode(false)` to `.with_legacy_session_mode(true)`, and COMPATIBILITY.md adds: `Compass does not impose a session-count cap; clients able to reach an unauthenticated server can allocate sessions until they expire.` The blocking `bounded-work` constraint requires all work over network responses to remain bounded.
findings.suggested_fix: Add and enforce a bounded maximum number of legacy sessions per server and return a distinct limit error when exhausted, or require authentication before allocating sessions.
